summaries.gardner: Synopsys has several Rule Breaker traits: it is a top dog in chip-design software with a durable advantage, strong management and a well-known backer (NVIDIA bought a $2B stake in December 2025). It misses on recent price momentum (about $430 in October 2026 versus $454 a year earlier) and on consumer brand recognition, and the stock is not widely called overvalued.
summaries.buffett: The business has a wide moat, recurring multi-year licences and high gross margins (77% in FY2025), which fits Buffett's taste for durable franchises. The $35B Ansys deal added about $10B of debt and $26.8B of goodwill, cutting returns on capital, and at roughly 108 times FY2026 GAAP EPS guidance there is no margin of safety.
summaries.munger: Munger would like the EDA duopoly with Cadence, the high switching costs and the indispensability to every advanced chip. Inverting, the main ways it fails are export controls, AI-driven disruption of design tools and overpaying for acquisitions, and the current price leaves little room for error.
summaries.lynch: Synopsys is a stalwart with fast-grower traits: management targets about 15% revenue CAGR and mid-20% non-GAAP EPS growth from FY2026 to FY2030. The story is easy to state, but the stock is well covered by Wall Street, the share count has risen with Ansys and NVIDIA issuance, and the non-GAAP P/E of about 28 roughly equals expected growth.
summaries.fisher: Synopsys fits Fisher well on R&D (over 25% of revenue), a pipeline of new products (Synopsys.ai, multi-die, Ansys simulation) and long-term orientation. Weaker points are recent GAAP margin compression after Ansys and a ~10% workforce cut that may test employee relations.
summaries.graham: Synopsys fails most of Graham's defensive tests: it pays no dividend, trades at about 108 times FY2026 GAAP EPS guidance and about 2.6 times book value. It is large and has grown EPS strongly over ten years, but it is not a Graham-style bargain.
summaries.thiel: Synopsys started with a monopoly-like position in logic synthesis and expanded into a full-flow EDA and IP franchise, with strong distribution to every major chipmaker. It does not have technology ten times better than Cadence, so it is closer to a durable duopoly than a Thiel-style monopoly, though its position should last decades.
summaries.gerstner: Synopsys is a beneficiary of the AI build-out (more and harder chips need more design software) and is moving into agentic AI with OpenAI and AWS deals. Its non-GAAP valuation (about 23 times FY2027 EPS estimates) and ~15% growth target fit his 'growth at a reasonable price' lens, but GAAP results, rising debt and flat share-price momentum are drawbacks.
summaries.druckenmiller: Earnings estimates are rising after the September 2026 investor day (FY2027 guidance of $11.1-11.2B revenue and $19.04-19.12 EPS beat consensus), a catalyst Druckenmiller looks for. But the stock has lagged the S&P 500 over the past year and five years, so price momentum does not yet confirm the story.
summaries.smith: Synopsys is a 'good company' by Fundsmith standards in gross margin, recurring revenue and resilience, but post-Ansys returns on capital are low, cash conversion is good, and Terry Smith would worry about the leverage and the large acquisition. Valuation is high on GAAP numbers.
summaries.greenblatt: On the Magic Formula Synopsys scores poorly: GAAP operating profit of about $0.8B over the last twelve months against an enterprise value near $89B gives an earnings yield of about 1%, and return on tangible capital is weak after Ansys. It would not appear on a Magic Formula screen.
summaries.akre: Akre's three legs: an extraordinary business (yes, a wide-moat duopoly), talented and honest management (largely yes, though Ghazi is new to the CEO role since 2024), and reinvestment at high rates (partly: R&D reinvestment is strong, but the $35B Ansys deal lowers returns). The fit is decent but not ideal.
summaries.pabrai: Pabrai's Dhandho approach seeks low-risk, high-uncertainty bargains, and Synopsys is neither cheap nor distressed at about $430 a share. The business is low-risk in the sense of permanent loss of franchise, but there is no large gap between price and value.
summaries.wood: Synopsys is an enabler of AI rather than an ARK-style disruptive platform: it profits from AI chip complexity and is building AI design agents. Its market is not likely to grow many times over in five years, so it fits ARK's themes only partly.
summaries.ackman: Synopsys meets many Ackman criteria: simple-to-describe, predictable, recurring, free-cash-flow-generative, with high barriers to entry. Leverage after Ansys and a full valuation are the main issues; it is not an obvious activist or deep-value opportunity.
summaries.sleep: Nick Sleep's scale-economies-shared model fits only partly: Synopsys's scale lets it out-invest rivals in R&D, but it captures savings as margin (targeting ~50% non-GAAP operating margin) rather than passing them to customers. Its long-term position looks secure but not clearly stronger in a decade.
summaries.valentine: Valentine looked for huge markets and painful problems; chip design complexity is a large, painful problem and Synopsys solves it. As a 40-year-old incumbent it is not a Sequoia-type early bet, but the market it serves keeps growing with AI.
summaries.nash: Synopsys passes Nash's quality and secular-trend tests (AI infrastructure layer, strong moat, revenue growth above 10%) but fails several hard rules: debt exceeds cash after Ansys, GAAP operating margin is below 20%, and operating expenses grew faster than revenue over the last year. His DCF at a 12% discount rate gives far less than today's price, and the 13-category score is about 65, below his 75 threshold.

momentum.evidence: The shares closed at $430.14 on October 23, 2026, down from about $454 in October 2025 and $483 in April 2026, while the S&P 500 rose about 11.5% from October 31, 2025 to 7,623.68.

g4.evidence: NVIDIA invested $2B at $414.79 a share in December 2025 and holds about 2.5%, and Synopsys signed AI deals with OpenAI and AWS (a multi-year IP licence worth over $1B) in 2026.

g6.evidence: 25 analysts rate it a consensus 'Strong Buy' with an average target of $586.95, about 36% above the price, so it is not commonly called overvalued.

simple.evidence: The model (multi-year software licences and IP royalties sold to chipmakers) is simple, but the technology and the Ansys integration take effort to understand.

b2.evidence: Revenue has risen every year from $3,685.3M in FY2020 to $7,054.2M in FY2025, though FY2025 included a guidance cut in its IP business.

integrity.evidence: Management is generally candid and pay is mostly stock-based, but law firms opened securities investigations after the September 2025 IP miss and the board approved a large dilutive acquisition.

b6.evidence: The $35B Ansys deal is strategic (silicon to systems) rather than empire-building, but it is a very large bet and followed by divestitures of non-core units (Optical Solutions, ARC processor IP).

roic.evidence: After Ansys, goodwill of $26.8B and intangibles of $11.5B sit on $47.7B of assets and FY2026 GAAP EPS guidance is only $3.84-4.08, so return on capital is now low and debt is $10.0B.

fcf.evidence: FY2025 operating cash flow of $1,518.6M less $169.5M capex gave about $1,349M of free cash flow, matching net income of $1,332.2M, and FY2026 FCF is guided at about $2.6B.

b10.evidence: Market value rose from about $51B in October 2021 to about $82B, but much of the increase came from issuing shares for Ansys and to NVIDIA rather than from retained earnings.

safety.evidence: At $430 the stock trades at about 28 times FY2026 non-GAAP EPS estimates and about 108 times GAAP EPS guidance, with no discount to a conservative value.

fairprice.evidence: About 23 times FY2027 non-GAAP EPS estimates ($18.73) for mid-20% EPS growth is reasonable for the quality, but GAAP earnings make it look expensive.

mu5.evidence: The duopoly and switching costs leave few ways to fail, but export controls, AI-driven disruption of design tools and leverage are real risks.

reinvest.evidence: Organic R&D (over 25% of revenue) earns high returns, but large reinvestment now goes into acquisitions like Ansys at lower returns.

ly2.evidence: It is a stalwart with fast-grower features: management targets about 15% revenue CAGR from FY2026 to FY2030 as AI chips get more complex.

ly3.evidence: The FY2026 non-GAAP P/E of about 28 is close to expected mid-20% EPS growth, but on GAAP EPS the P/E is far above the growth rate.

runway.evidence: AI, automotive and multi-die chips plus Ansys simulation give room for years of growth, with segment targets of at least 13% (EDA) and 17% (IP) annual growth.

ly7.evidence: Diluted shares rose from 155.9M in FY2024 to 192.3M in Q3 FY2026 after Ansys and the NVIDIA placement, and recent insider transactions are sales, not purchases.

ly8.evidence: Synopsys is heavily covered (25 analysts) and about 93% institutionally owned.

fi2.evidence: It keeps launching new lines such as Synopsys.ai, multi-die design tools and AI design agents, and added Ansys simulation in 2025.

fi3.evidence: R&D of $2,134.8M in the first nine months of FY2026 supports leading tools such as Fusion Compiler and PrimeTime that are used on most advanced chips.

fi4.evidence: Its enterprise sales force secures large multi-year deals (backlog $11.4B at FY2025 end, the AWS licence over $1B), but selling is relationship-driven rather than unusually innovative.

longterm.evidence: It spends more than 25% of revenue on R&D and made a multi-decade bet on 'silicon to systems' with Ansys despite near-term earnings dilution.

gr1.evidence: Synopsys is an S&P 500 company with FY2026 revenue guided at $9.69-9.74B and a market value of roughly $82B.

ni10.evidence: It has reported annual profits throughout the last decade, including net income of $664.3M in FY2020 and $1,332.2M in FY2025.

gr4.evidence: Synopsys does not pay a dividend.

eps10.evidence: Diluted EPS rose from $4.27 in FY2020 to $8.04 in FY2025, already well above a one-third increase.

gr6.evidence: At $430 the price is far above 15 times average earnings (FY2025 diluted EPS was $8.04 and FY2026 GAAP guidance is $3.84-4.08).

gr7.evidence: With a GAAP P/E near 100 and price/book of about 2.6 (equity $31.2B), the product is far above 22.5.

th1.evidence: Its tools are best-in-class in areas like timing signoff and interface IP, but not ten times better than Cadence's.

timing.evidence: AI chips, chiplets and 2nm-class nodes are raising design complexity just as Synopsys adds AI agents and Ansys multiphysics simulation.

th3.evidence: Founded in 1986 around logic synthesis (Design Compiler), it dominated that niche and expanded into full EDA flows, IP and now simulation.

team.evidence: CEO Sassine Ghazi is a 25-year Synopsys engineer-operator who closed the Ansys deal, and co-founder Aart de Geus built the company, but Ghazi's CEO record is short (since 2024).

th5.evidence: It has a direct enterprise sales and support force embedded with every major chipmaker and foundry.

durable.evidence: The EDA duopoly has held for decades and foundry certifications plus engineer training make displacement within 10-20 years unlikely, though AI tools could reshape pricing.

th7.evidence: The 'silicon to systems' combination of EDA and Ansys simulation is a distinctive bet, but Cadence is pursuing the same idea.

trend.evidence: Every AI accelerator from NVIDIA, AMD and hyperscalers is designed with EDA tools, and NVIDIA's $2B investment and the AWS and OpenAI deals tie Synopsys to the AI build-out.

dr1.evidence: FY2027 guidance ($19.04-19.12 non-GAAP EPS) came in above the $17.81 consensus at the September 2026 investor day, and BofA raised FY2027 EPS estimates by 7%.

dr2.evidence: Ansys synergies, margin expansion toward ~44% non-GAAP operating margin in FY2027 and IP recovery should improve results, though much is already in guidance.

dr4.evidence: Lower rates would ease the cost of about $10.0B of debt, but demand depends mainly on chip-industry spending rather than macro liquidity.

dr6.evidence: Catalysts include Q4 FY2026 results in December, about $1B of planned buybacks, the AWS IP deal and Ansys cost synergies.

dr7.evidence: The franchise quality supports conviction, but leverage, export-control risk and weak momentum argue against a very concentrated position.

gm.evidence: GAAP gross margin was 77.0% in FY2025 (79.7% in FY2024) even after Ansys amortisation.

fcfyield.evidence: FY2026 FCF guidance of about $2.6B against a market value near $82B is a yield of about 3.2%, fair but not cheap for mid-teens growth.

gb2.evidence: GAAP operating income of about $0.8B over the last twelve months is only about 1% of an enterprise value near $89B.

pa2.evidence: The FY2025 setback (China export curbs and a struggling foundry customer hitting Design IP) looks temporary: Design IP returned to year-over-year growth in Q3 FY2026.

pa4.evidence: The duopoly position and recurring licences make permanent loss of the franchise unlikely, though valuation losses are possible.

wo1.evidence: It is a key enabler of AI chips and builds AI design agents (Synopsys.ai, OpenAI deal), but it is not itself an AI platform leader.

wo2.evidence: Software licence prices are not falling with volume in a way that opens big new demand.

wo3.evidence: It combines AI with simulation and chip design, but not several of ARK's core platforms.

wo4.evidence: Management's own target is about 15% annual revenue growth to FY2030, far from a many-fold expansion.

ac3.evidence: It has no commodity exposure, but is exposed to the semiconductor cycle, US-China trade policy and interest on about $10.0B of debt.

ns1.evidence: Synopsys keeps scale gains as margin, targeting about 50% non-GAAP operating margin by FY2030, rather than cutting prices.

ns4.evidence: Ansys and AI agents could strengthen its position, but Cadence, Siemens and AI-native startups are competing hard for the same opportunity.

va2.evidence: Designing and verifying chips with tens of billions of transistors without costly re-spins is a large, painful problem for every chipmaker.

tn1.evidence: It sells into AI infrastructure (the tools behind every AI chip), but it is a 1986 EDA company adapting to AI rather than one built for it.

tn2.evidence: The market sees an EDA tool vendor, while management is building a 'silicon to systems' simulation and AI-agent platform with Ansys and OpenAI.

tn3.evidence: It is a large-cap US software company, outside all the zones to avoid.

tn4.evidence: Revenue has grown every year and it is profitable; it misses on cash versus debt ($3.6B vs $10.0B) for a valid reason, the debt-funded Ansys acquisition.

tn5.evidence: Free cash flow has been positive, but debt has exceeded cash every quarter since the Ansys deal closed in July 2025.

tn6.evidence: FY2026 revenue is guided at $9.69-9.74B, up about 38% (helped by Ansys), and FY2027 guidance implies about 15% growth.

tn7.evidence: FY2026 guided revenue growth of about 38% plus an FCF margin of about 27% ($2.6B/$9.7B) is far above 40, though inflated by the acquisition.

tn8.evidence: In the first nine months of FY2026 revenue rose 49% but operating income fell to $681.0M from $793.5M, so expenses grew faster.

tn9.evidence: It hits two instant kills: debt ($10.0B) exceeds cash ($3.6B) and GAAP operating margin (13.0% in FY2025, 9.5% in 9M FY2026) is below 20%.

tn10.evidence: US export controls on EDA sales to China (curbs imposed in May 2025), BIS subpoenas and securities investigations after the 2025 miss are live risks.

tn11.evidence: Synopsys provides chip-design software, IP and simulation that help chipmakers and system makers build working products faster, charging multi-year time-based licences and IP fees.

tn13.evidence: Score about 65: cash vs debt 0, revenue growth 10, operating margin 0, short interest 10 (3.4%), institutions 10 (93%), revenue vs expenses 0, 5-year return vs S&P 500 0, moat 10, CEO 5, pricing power 10, secular trend 10, culture and mission 5, talent 5.

tn14.evidence: Revenue grew every year, but GAAP operating margin fell from 24.9% (FY2022) to 13.0% (FY2025), operating cash flow fell in FY2023-FY2024, and debt exceeded cash in FY2025.

tn15.evidence: Nine-month FY2026 operating income of $681.0M covers interest of $429.3M only 1.6 times, and assets excluding goodwill ($20.9B) are about 1.3 times liabilities ($16.6B), though the current ratio is 1.3.

tn18.evidence: Ghazi has been CEO only since 2024, is not a founder and has made no notable open-market share purchases.

tn20.evidence: Q3 FY2026 beat consensus (non-GAAP EPS $3.91 vs about $3.66), but Q3 FY2025 missed badly on revenue and EPS.

tn21.evidence: Red flags include declining GAAP margins after the Ansys deal and insider sales with no purchases, though there is no sign of fraud or auditor change.

tn22.evidence: It has about $9.7B of revenue, strong cash flow and real profits; the NVIDIA share sale was strategic, not a cash-raising habit.

tn24.evidence: A ~3.2% FCF yield implies roughly low-teens long-term FCF growth, about what management targets (mid-20% FCF growth to FY2030), so the price is roughly in line with expected delivery.

tn25.evidence: Using 3-year averages (about 15% revenue growth, 22.8% FCF margin), 5 years of FCF, 4% terminal growth and a 12% discount rate, less net debt of $6.4B, gives about $136 a share, well below $430.

tn26.evidence: It passes the Rule of 40 and its forward non-GAAP P/E of about 28 is below Cadence's (about 38), with a PEG near 1.0 on FY2027 EPS growth of about 24%.
